text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The trade unions in the mining sector oppose economic reforms, the paper says.
- Depreciation of the leu national currency affected the tourism sector.
- President Emil Constantinescu rejected allegations saying the parties in the ruling coalition plan to control state banks and public utilities.
- Seasonal works in the farming sector proceed at slow pace, the paper says.
- Police investigations showed that losses related to tax evasion allegedly committed by local businessman Zaher Iskandarani amounted to some 1,000 billion lei.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Poverty has pushed many Romanians to travel to Yugoslavia to donate blood in exchange for money, the paper says.
- Investigations showed that the alleged irregularities in the case of Iskandarani amount to threats to national security, the paper says.
- Renel RA electricity authority halted power supplies to the Moldova Noua coalfield following its failure to pay old debts.
- Red tape in Romania keeps foreign investors away, the paper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Jail terms for money laundering will amount to up to 12 years according to a draft law issued by the Interior Ministry.
- Parliament will start debates on the 1997 budget on Wednesday, the paper says.
General:
ADEVARUL
- Jail sentences against journalists are too severe a form of punishment, said Justice Minister Valeriu Stoica. He said the new criminal code would be adjusted to the European system.

- Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma said he wanted to meet Romanian President Emil Constantinescu to solve the problems between the two states after the last round of negotiations on the bilatertal treaty produced no results.
- The national council fighting corruption discussed the stage of investigations in one of the three major cases of "cigarette, coffee and alcohol mafia" which caused losses worth 1.0 billion lei.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Money laundering crimes would carry sentences of up to 12 years in jail under a draft of law which acknowledges this kind of crime for the first time in Romania.

- The former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) wants neither to bring down the present government nor enter the ruling coalition, said PDSR president Ion Iliescu. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
